questions.question: A few sentences of a paragraph are given below. While the first and last sentences, numbered 1 and 6, are in correct order, the sentences in between are jumbled up. Arrange these sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. 1. The festival of Pongal, celebrated in Tamil Nadu, is dedicated to Surya (the Sun god), and corresponds to the harvest festival of Makara Sankaranti, observed across India. P. This milk ritual gives the festival its name and the festival gives the prasad (a devotional offering made to God and later shared among devotees) its name. Q. Despite varying food habits of different ecological zones of Tamil Nadu, which vary from fish curry on the coast to goat curry inland, Pongal celebrations and prasad is consistent across the region. R. The prasad has two versions, the sweet (made of coconut and jaggery) and the salted (a khichri of moong dal and rice, dripping with ghee and sprinkled with cashew-nuts and peppercorns). S. Pongal literally means 'boiling over' in Tamil, and comes from the ritual of letting milk boil over in a new pot as a sign of abundance. 6. For example, Kolam, (elaborate patterns of rice flour outside the door). whether outside rural huts or palatial bungalows, are as commonplace as the two versions of the prasad prepared in all households.
questions.questionHtml:
A few sentences of a paragraph are given below. While the first and last sentences, numbered 1 and 6, are in correct order, the sentences in between are jumbled up. Arrange these sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

1. The festival of Pongal, celebrated in Tamil Nadu, is dedicated to Surya (the Sun god), and corresponds to the harvest festival of Makara Sankaranti, observed across India.

P. This milk ritual gives the festival its name and the festival gives the prasad (a devotional offering made to God and later shared among devotees) its name.

Q. Despite varying food habits of different ecological zones of Tamil Nadu, which vary from fish curry on the coast to goat curry inland, Pongal celebrations and prasad is consistent across the region.

R. The prasad has two versions, the sweet (made of coconut and jaggery) and the salted (a khichri of moong dal and rice, dripping with ghee and sprinkled with cashew-nuts and peppercorns).

S. Pongal literally means 'boiling over' in Tamil, and comes from the ritual of letting milk boil over in a new pot as a sign of abundance.

6. For example, Kolam, (elaborate patterns of rice flour outside the door). whether outside rural huts or palatial bungalows, are as commonplace as the two versions of the prasad prepared in all households.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1SPRQ6'.

Key Points

  • The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
  • We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'. 
  • Sentence S will be the first sentence because it is an introductory sentence telling us about the festival of Pongal.
  • Sentence P will be the next sentence because it further explains the milk ritual.
  • Sentence R will be the next sentence because it explains the prasad which is being discussed in Sentence P.
  • Lastly, Sentence Q will be used.
  • Thus, the correct sequence is:
    • S: Pongal literally means 'boiling over' in Tamil, and comes from the ritual of letting milk boil over in a new pot as a sign of abundance.
    • P: This milk ritual gives the festival its name and the festival gives the prasad (a devotional offering made to God and later shared among devotees) its name.
    • R: The prasad has two versions, the sweet (made of coconut and jaggery) and the salted (a khichri of moong dal and rice, dripping with ghee and sprinkled with cashew-nuts and peppercorns).
    • Q: Despite varying food habits of different ecological zones of Tamil Nadu, which vary from fish curry on the coast to goat curry inland, Pongal celebrations and prasad is consistent across the region.
       

Correct Sequence: The festival of Pongal, celebrated in Tamil Nadu, is dedicated to Surya (the Sun god), and corresponds to the harvest festival of Makara Sankaranti, observed across India. Pongal literally means 'boiling over' in Tamil, and comes from the ritual of letting milk boil over in a new pot as a sign of abundance. This milk ritual gives the festival its name and the festival gives the prasad (a devotional offering made to God and later shared among devotees) its name. The prasad has two versions, the sweet (made of coconut and jaggery) and the salted (a khichri of moong dal and rice, dripping with ghee and sprinkled with cashew-nuts and peppercorns). Despite varying food habits of different ecological zones of Tamil Nadu, which vary from fish curry on the coast to goat curry inland, Pongal celebrations and prasad is consistent across the region. For example, Kolam, (elaborate patterns of rice flour outside the door). whether outside rural huts or palatial bungalows, are as commonplace as the two versions of the prasad prepared in all households.

questions.question: Directions: In this section, each item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences in each have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly on the answer sheet. S1: Imitation is not civilization. S6: When a man has begun to be ashamed of his ancestors, the end has come. P: As ass in a lion's skin never makes a lion Q: It is verily the sign of awful degradation in a man. R: Cowardly imitation never makes for progress. S: When a man has begun to hate himself; then the last blow has come.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: In this section, each item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences in each have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly on the answer sheet.

S1: Imitation is not civilization. 

S6: When a man has begun to be ashamed of his ancestors, the end has come.  

P: As ass in a lion's skin never makes a lion

Q: It is verily the sign of awful degradation in a man.  

R: Cowardly imitation never makes for progress. 

S: When a man has begun to hate himself; then the last blow has come.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "PRQS"

Key Points

  • Sentence S1 states that imitation is not civilization.
  • Sentence P compares a person who tries to imitate something they are not to an ass wearing a lion's skin, saying that it never makes a lion.
  • Sentence R emphasizes that cowardly imitation never leads to progress.
  • Sentence Q characterizes the act of imitation as a sign of degradation in a person.
  • Sentence S states that when a person begins to hate themselves, it is a sign that the end has come.
  • Sentence S6 adds that when a person begins to be ashamed of their ancestors, it is also a sign that the end has come.
  • When the sentences are put in this order, they form a coherent and logical paragraph about the dangers of imitation and the importance of self-respect and pride in one's ancestors.

Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.

Correct paragraph: S1 Imitation is not civilization. P As ass in a lion's skin never makes a lion. R Cowardly imitation never makes for progress. Q It is verily the sign of awful degradation in a man. S When a man has begun to hate himself; then the 1ast blow has come. S6 When a man has begun to be ashamed of his ancestors, the end has come.

questions.question: Direction: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. It is time to take tea.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

It is time to take tea.

options.text: It is time for the tea to be taken
options.html: It is time for the tea to be taken

options.text: It is time tea must have been taken.
options.html: It is time tea must have been taken.

options.text: It is time we should take the tea.
options.html: It is time we should take the tea.

options.text: It is time the tea has to be taken by us.
options.html: It is time the tea has to be taken by us.

questions.solution: The sentence is in active voice with the subject "it" and the verb "to take." To convert it into passive voice, we need to make the object (tea) the subject and use the passive form of the verb "to take" (be taken). Structure: It is time for + Object + to be V3. (Passive Voice). Correct sentence: It is time for the tea to be taken.

questions.solution: The rule for changing the given sentence from the Active voice to Passive voice: Interchange the object and subject with each other, i.e. object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence. Structure: Object + should + be + V3 + by Subject (Passive Voice). "Should" is a modal verb. They are used with the base form of the main verb (They should go; I should ask her). Correct sentence: The job should be applied for before the deadline.

questions.question: What should come in the place of blank number (1)?

questions.solution:

Key Points
  • The sentence reads: “Successful entrepreneurs often display resilience, creativity, and the capacity to (1) ______ uncertainty.”

  • “Navigate” means to manage or deal with a difficult situation effectively, which fits perfectly in the context of handling uncertainty in business.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice. She said to the technician, "If you fix my laptop today, I will recommend you to my friends."
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.


She said to the technician, "If you fix my laptop today, I will recommend you to my friends."

options.text: She told the technician that if he fixed her laptop that day, she would recommend him to her friends.
options.html: She told the technician that if he fixed her laptop that day, she would recommend him to her friends.

options.text: She told the technician that if he fixes her laptop today, she will recommend him to her friends.
options.html: She told the technician that if he fixes her laptop today, she will recommend him to her friends.

options.text: She told the technician that if he fixed her laptop today, she will recommend him to her friends.
options.html: She told the technician that if he fixed her laptop today, she will recommend him to her friends.

options.text: She told the technician that if he fixes her laptop that day, she would recommend him to her friends.
options.html: She told the technician that if he fixes her laptop that day, she would recommend him to her friends.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • Indirect Speech: She told the technician that if he fixed her laptop that day, she would recommend him to her friends.
  • Key Conversions:
    • Pronoun changes: "you" becomes "he" (the technician), "my" becomes "her", "I" becomes "she", "you" (object) becomes "him".
    • Tense changes:
      • "fix" (present) → "fixed" (past simple).
      • "will recommend" → "would recommend".
    • Time expression: "today" becomes "that day" in indirect speech.
    • Reporting verb: "said to" changes to "told".
  • Punctuation and Format:
    • Quotation marks are removed in indirect speech.
    • Conditional structure is retained.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: She told the technician that if he fixed her laptop that day, she would recommend him to her friends.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 2: No tense or time change ("fixes", "today", "will recommend" should be "fixed", "that day", "would recommend").
  • Option 3: Only partial tense change ("today" remains, "will recommend" remains; should be "that day", "would recommend").
  • Option 4: Only partial tense change ("fixes" should be "fixed").

questions.question: What is the term for the shock felt when plunging into cold water?

questions.question: Select the word that is closest in meaning (SYNONYM) to the word given below. Deride
questions.questionHtml:

Deride
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Mock'.
 
Key Points
  • 'Deride' means to express contempt or ridicule towards somebody/something. (उपहास/ तिरस्कार करना)
    • Example: His colleagues often derided his decision to leave a high-paying job for social service.
  • The correct word 'Mock' means to make fun of or ridicule, often in a scornful manner. (उपहासित/मज़ाक उड़ाना)
    • Example: The kids mock the new boy because of his accent.
  • Hence, the correct synonym of 'Deride' is 'Mock'.
Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 1".
 
Additional Information
  • 'Blame' means to assign responsibility for a fault or wrong. (दोष देना). But it does not fit the context of deride; hence, it's not chosen.
  • 'Inspire' means to fill someone with the urge or ability to do or feel something (प्रेरित करना), which is not synonymous with deride.
  • 'Defend' means to protect from harm or danger. (बचाव करना/रक्षा करना). This also does not match the context of deride, and hence is not chosen.

questions.question: Each of the following question consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences in each have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. Find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mar your response accordingly. S1: Mount Vesuvius, a volcano located between the ancient Italian cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum, has received much attention because of its frequent and destructive eruptions. P: The volcano had been inactive for centuries. Q: Although one account unearthed by archaeologists says that a hard rain and a strong wind had disturbed the celestial calm during the preceding night. R: There was little warning of the coming eruption. S: The most famous of these eruptions occurred in A.D. 79. S6: Early the next morning, the volcano poured a huge river of molten rock down upon Herculaneum, completely burying the city and filling the harbor with coagulated lava.
questions.questionHtml:
Each of the following question consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences in each have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. Find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mar your response accordingly.

S1: Mount Vesuvius, a volcano located between the ancient Italian cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum, has received much attention because of its frequent and destructive eruptions.

P: The volcano had been inactive for centuries.

Q: Although one account unearthed by archaeologists says that a hard rain and a strong wind had disturbed the celestial calm during the preceding night.

R: There was little warning of the coming eruption. 

S: The most famous of these eruptions occurred in A.D. 79.  

S6: Early the next morning, the volcano poured a huge river of molten rock down upon Herculaneum, completely burying the city and filling the harbor with coagulated lava.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: SPRQ

Key Points

  • Here, the first and last sentences are given.
  • Thus, it becomes easy to identify the second and fifth sentences.
  • The second sentence would be the continuation of the first.
  • Here, the first sentence mentions Mount Vesuvius'.
  • The second sentence is S, as it mentions the occurrence of the eruption, which is a continuation of the first sentence.
  • The third sentence is P and the fourth sentence is R.
  • The fifth sentence is Q, which mentions the cause of the eruption.
  • Thus, option 3 is correct.

The correct passage is: Mount Vesuvius, a volcano located between the ancient Italian cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum, has received much attention because of its frequent and destructive eruptions. The most famous of these eruptions occurred in A.D. 79. The volcano had been inactive for centuries. There was little warning of the coming eruption, although one account unearthed by archaeologists says that a hard rain and a strong wind had disturbed the celestial calm during the preceding night. Early the next morning, the volcano poured a huge river of molten rock down upon Herculaneum, completely burying the city and filling the harbor with coagulated lava.

questions.questionHtml:
Select the alternative which best express the meaning of the idioms/phrase.

Akin to
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Similar to something.

Key Points

  • The phrase "akin to" means similar to something or having similar qualities. (के समान)
    • Example: The two languages are closely akin to each other.
  • "Similar to something" means something that resembles or has a likeness to another thing. (कुछ के समान)
    • Example: Her smile is similar to her mother's.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Similar to something.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Different from (अलग से): Not the same as another or each other.
    • Example: His opinion is different from mine.
  • Indifferent to (उदासीन): Having no particular interest or sympathy; unconcerned.
    • Example: She seemed indifferent to the results of the game.
  • Attention to (ध्यान देना): The act of focusing on something or someone.
    • Example: Please pay attention to the instructions given.

questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice:

The mother said to her children, "Before going out to play, make sure you finish your homework and tidy up your rooms as I instructed you this morning."

options.text: The mother told her children that before going out to play, they should make sure to finish their homework and tidy up their rooms as she had instructed them that morning.

options.text: The mother told her children that before going out to play, they must make sure they finished their homework and tidied up their rooms as she had instructed them this morning.
options.html: The mother told her children that before going out to play, they must make sure they finished their homework and tidied up their rooms as she had instructed them this morning.

options.text: The mother told her children before going out to play, make sure you finish your homework and tidy up your rooms as she had instructed you that morning.
options.html: The mother told her children before going out to play, make sure you finish your homework and tidy up your rooms as she had instructed you that morning.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • Indirect Speech: The mother told her children that before going out to play, they should make sure to finish their homework and tidy up their rooms as she had instructed them that morning.
  • Key Conversions:
    • Pronoun changes: "you" becomes "they/them", "your" becomes "their", "I" becomes "she", "you" (object) becomes "them".
    • Time reference: "this morning" becomes "that morning" in indirect speech.
    • Verb changes: "make sure you finish" becomes "make sure to finish" to fit the indirect structure naturally. Modality "should" is correctly used for polite commands or advice.
    • Reporting verb: "said to" changes to "told".
  • Punctuation and Format:
    • Quotation marks are removed in indirect speech.
    • Imperative and reporting structures are preserved.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: The mother told her children that before going out to play, they should make sure to finish their homework and tidy up their rooms as she had instructed them that morning.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 2: Incorrect pronoun usage ("you", "your", "you" instead of "they", "their", "them") and "this morning" is not changed.
  • Option 3: Inconsistent verb tenses and "this morning" not changed to "that morning".
  • Option 4: Direct speech structure retained and pronoun/time changes missing.
